and its evidence is His saying: "And by the night when it is still," so He contrasted it with the night. Its parallel is His saying: "that Our punishment comes to them in the forenoon" (duhan), meaning in the daytime. Qatada and Muqatil said: it means the time of forenoon (al-duha), which is the hour when the sun rises high and the day is balanced between heat and cold in winter and summer. It was said: it is the hour in which Allah spoke to Musa. It was said: it is the hour in which the magicians were thrown down prostrate. Its explanation is His saying: "and that the people be gathered in the forenoon." The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said regarding this and similar expressions: it is by supposing a Lord, the meaning being: "and the Lord of the forenoon."

"And by the night when it is still." Al-Hasan said: "it comes with its darkness." This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas; al-Walibi from him: "when it departs." al-Dahhak: "it covers everything." Mujahid, Qatada and Ibn Zayd: "it becomes calm with creation and its darkness settles." It is said: a "night saj" and a "sea saj" when it is still. The rajiz said:
"How good is the moonlit night and the still night, and a path like the cloth of the weaver."

And the poet of Banu Tha'laba said:
"What is our fault if the sea of your cousin's son surges, while your sea is still, hiding nothing of the vanquished?"

"Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He hated you." That is, He has not left you since He chose you, nor has He hated you since He loved you. This is the answer to the oath.

"And the Hereafter is better for you than the first, and your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be satisfied." It was said: of reward; and it was said: of victory, establishment, and the multiplication of believers.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Amir al-Samarqandi informed us, saying: Umar ibn Bahr narrated to us, saying: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Qutayba, from Sufyan, from al-Awza'i, from Isma'il ibn Abd Allah, from Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Abbas [from his father], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw what will be opened to my nation after me, victory after victory," and that pleased me. So it was revealed: "And your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be satisfied." He said: "He will give me in Paradise a thousand palaces of pearls, its dust being musk, in each palace what is fitting for him."

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them from Ibn Jarir, who said: Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: al-Hakam ibn Zahr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "And your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be satisfied," he said: the satisfaction of Muhammad is that no one of his family members enters the Fire. It was also said: it is intercession for all believers.

Abu Abd Allah al-Qanjawi informed me, saying: Abu Ali al-Muqri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Asad al-Mawsili narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Maddadi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, saying: Harb ibn Surayh al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: my paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hanafiyya narrated to me, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will intercede for my nation until my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, calls out: 'Are you pleased, O Muhammad?' and I say: 'My Lord, I am pleased.'" Then he said to me: "You people of Iraq say that the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an is: 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah.'" I said: "Indeed, we say that." He said: "But we, the People of the House, say that the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, Exalted is He, is: 'And your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be satisfied,' and it is intercession."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir ibn Sa'dan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salih al-Misri narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Bakr ibn Sawada narrated to him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited Allah's saying concerning Ibrahim: "Whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful," and the saying of Isa: "If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise." Then he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, my nation, my nation," and wept.

Allah, glorified is He, said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad — and your Lord knows best — and ask him what makes him weep." Jibril came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed him. Allah, glorified is He, said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad and say: Indeed We will please you regarding your nation, and We will not grieve you."

It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, when this verse was revealed: "Then I will not be pleased while one of my nation is in the Fire."

Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon Fatima (may Allah be pleased with her), and she was wearing a garment of camel hide, grinding with her hand and nursing her child. The eyes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) shed tears when he saw her, and he said: "O my daughter, hasten the bitterness of this world for the sweetness of the Hereafter, for Allah has revealed to me: 'And your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be satisfied.'"

Then Allah, glorified is He, informed of his state (peace be upon him) before revelation, and reminded him of His blessings, saying, Mighty is He and Exalted: "Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?"

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Nisaburi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Abu Umar al-Hawdi and Abu al-Rabi al-Zahrani narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord a request that I wished I had not asked. I said: 'O Lord, You gave Sulayman ibn Dawud a great kingdom, and You gave so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such.' He said: 'O Muhammad, did I not find you an orphan and give you refuge?' I said: 'Yes, my Lord.' He said: 'Did I not find you lost and guide you?' I said: 'Yes, my Lord.' He said: 'Did I not find you poor and make you rich?' I said: 'Yes, my Lord.'"

The meaning of the verse: "Did He not find you an orphan": young, poor, weak, when your two parents died, and they had left you no wealth nor shelter. So He made for you a shelter to which you could resort and a dwelling in which you could stay, and He joined you to your uncle Abu Talib until he raised you well and sufficed you in your needs.

I heard the teacher Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Nasr Mansur ibn Abd Allah al-Isfahani say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Iskandarani say: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Malati say: I heard my father say: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida say: I heard my father say: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq was asked: Why was the Prophet (ﷺ) made an orphan from his parents? He said: "So that there would be no right upon him for any created being."

And I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Anbari relate with a chain of his which I do not remember, from Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, from his father, that he said regarding the Exalted saying: "Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge": it is from the sayings of the Arabs: "a pearl that is unique (durra yatima)" when it has no equal. And it has come in poetry:
"Nor a pearl unique, a sea...
glittering in the merchant's satchel."

So the meaning of the verse is: "Did He not find you unique in your nobility and your virtue, without peer, and so He gave you refuge with Himself."

Ashhab al-Aqili read "fa-awa" with shortening, meaning: "He had mercy on you." The Arabs say: "I gave refuge (awaytu) to so-and-so (li-fulan)," meaning "I had mercy on him."

"And He found you lost," meaning concerning what you are upon today, and He guided you to what you are upon today.

Al-Suddi said: "He was upon the affair of his people for forty years." Al-Kalbi said: "He found you among a misguided people, and guided you to monotheism and prophethood." It was also said: "and He guided them through you." Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Shahr ibn Hawshab and Ibn Kaysan said: "He found you lost (dallan)," from the landmarks of prophethood and the rulings of the Sharia, unaware of them, and He guided you to them. Its parallel and evidence is His saying: "And indeed you were, before it, among the unaware," and His saying: "You did not know what the Book was, nor faith." It was also said: "lost (dallan)" in the valleys of Makkah, and He guided you to your grandfather Abd al-Muttalib and returned you to him.

Abu al-Duha narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got lost while he was a small child in the valleys of Makkah, and Abu Jahl saw him returning from his flocks, and returned him to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib. Allah, glorified is He, bestowed His favor upon him in that, when He returned him to his grandfather by the hand of his enemy.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus informed us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Awf narrated to us, saying: Khalid informed us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Bishr ibn Sa'id, from his father, who said: I performed Hajj in the Jahiliyya, and behold, a man was circumambulating the House, chanting verses and saying:
"O Lord, return my riding camel, Muhammad; return him to me and do me a favor."
I asked: "Who is this?" It was said: "Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim. His camels went astray, and he sent his grandson in search of them, and he never sent him on any errand but that he returned with it, but he was delayed." He said: "I had not gone far when the Prophet (ﷺ) came with the camels, and he said: 'O my son, I have grieved over you with a grief that will never leave me.'"

And in the hadith of Ka'b al-Ahbar concerning the birth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the beginning of his affair: when Halima had fulfilled the duty of nursing, she brought the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to return him to Abd al-Muttalib. Halima said: "I set out walking until I reached the great gate of the gates of Makkah, and I heard a caller calling: 'Congratulations to you, O valley of Makkah! Today the light, the religion, the splendor and the beauty will return to you.'" She said: "Then I set down the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to attend to a need and fix my clothes, and I heard a severe crash. I turned and did not see him, so I said: 'O people, where is the boy?' They said: 'Which of the boys?'"

I said: "Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, by whom Allah brightened my face and enriched my poverty. I raised him until, when I attained in him my joy and hope, I came to return him, and this one takes from my trust, snatched from before my eyes before his foot touched the ground. By al-Lat and al-Uzza, if I do not see him I will throw myself from the top of the mountain, and I will surely cut myself into pieces."

They said: "We have seen nothing." When they despaired of me, I put my hand on the top of my head and said: "Alas Muhammad! Alas my son!" The virgin girls wept at my weeping, and the people cried out with me in grief for me. Then behold, an old man like a withered one leaning on a staff said: "What is wrong with you, O Sa'diyya?"

I said: "I have lost my son Muhammad." He said: "Do not weep. I will direct you to one who knows his knowledge, and if he wishes to return him, he will do so." I said: "May my soul be your ransom, and who is he?" He said: "The greatest idol, Hubal."

She said: He entered and I was watching. He circumambulated Hubal, kissed its head and called out: "O my master! Your favor upon Quraysh has been ancient, and this Sa'diyya claims that a son of hers has gone astray, so return him if you wish, and remove this desolation from the valley of Makkah, for she claims that her son Muhammad has gone astray." He said: Hubal fell on its face, and the idols toppled, and it said: "Away from us, O old man! Our destruction is at the hand of Muhammad."

She said: Then the old man came, and I heard the chattering of his teeth and the trembling of his knee, and he had thrown his staff from his hand, saying: "O Halima, your son has a Lord who will not neglect him, so seek him gently." She said: I feared the news would reach Abd al-Muttalib before me, so I went to him. When he looked at me he said: "Did a fortunate one come to you, or an unlucky one?" I said: "Rather, the greatest misfortune." He understood it from me and said: "Perhaps your son went astray from you." I said: "Yes." He supposed that some of Quraysh had seized him. Abd al-Muttalib drew his sword, no one could stand before him from the intensity of his anger, and he called out at the top of his voice: "O family of Ghalib, O family of Ghalib!" — and this was their call in the Jahiliyya — and all of Quraysh answered him, and they said: "What is your story?" He said: "My son Muhammad is lost." Quraysh said: "Mount, and we will mount with you. If you climb a mountain, we will climb it with you; if you plunge into a sea, we will plunge with you." He mounted, Quraysh mounted with him, and he took the high part of Makkah and descended to its low part. When he saw nothing, he left the people, wrapped himself and donned another garment, and came to the Sacred House. He circumambulated seven times, then began to say:
"O Lord, return my riding camel Muhammad; return him, my Lord, and do me a favor.
O Lord, Muhammad has not been found, the gathering of my people all scattered."

Then we heard a caller calling from the air: "O people, do not cry out, for Muhammad has a Lord who will not forsake him or neglect him." Abd al-Muttalib said: "O you who call, who is with us, and where is he?" He said: "In the valley of Tihama, by the tree of Yemen."

Abd al-Muttalib came mounted and armed. When he reached part of the way, Waraqa ibn Nawfal met him, and they went together. While they were thus, behold, the Prophet (ﷺ) was standing under a tree, pulling its branches and playing with its leaves. Abd al-Muttalib said to him: "Who are you, boy?"

He said: "I am Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib." Abd al-Muttalib said: "May my soul be your ransom, I am your grandfather." Then he carried him on the front of his saddle and returned him to Makkah, and Quraysh were reassured after that.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out with his uncle Abu Talib in the caravan of Maysara, the slave of Khadija. While he was riding one dark night on a camel, Iblis came, seized the camel's reins, and turned him away from the road. Then Jibril came, blew upon Iblis a blast by which he fell as far as Abyssinia, and returned him to the caravan. Allah bestowed His favor upon him in that.

It was said: "And He found you lost" refers to the night of the Ascension, when Jibril left you and you did not know the way, and He guided you to the lote-tree of the Throne.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish narrated to me, saying: Some people of theology said regarding His saying:

And He found you lost and guided you: when the Arabs find a tree alone in a wilderness of the earth, with no second one beside it, they call it "ḍāllah" (a lone tree), and they find their way to the road by it.

He said: "And He found you lost and guided you" means: alone, with no prophet other than you, so I guided the creation to Me through you. ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Tirmidhi said: "And He found you obscure, not mentioned and not known, who you were, so He guided them to you until they knew you, and informed them of what He had bestowed upon you."

Bassam ibn ʿAbdullah said: "And He found you lost" means: lost regarding yourself, not knowing who you were, so He made you know yourself and your state. Abu Bakr al-Warraq and others said: "And He found you lost" means: lost in love for Abu Talib, so He guided you to love of Him. Others said: "He found you loving, so He guided you to the One you love." The evidence for this is His saying, relating of the brothers of Joseph: ﴿Indeed, our father is in clear error﴾ [Surah Yusuf 12:8], and His saying: ﴿By Allah, you are surely in your old error﴾ [Surah Yusuf 12:95], meaning: the excess of love for Joseph.

It was also said: "We found you forgetful regarding the matter of the exception (istithna')" when you were asked about the People of the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿that one of them may forget (tadilla) [the other]﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 2:282], meaning: forget. Sahl said: "He found your self to be the self of desire and nature, so He turned it toward the path of knowledge and the Sharia." Junayd said: "He found you perplexed regarding the explanation of the Book revealed to you, so He guided you to its explanation," based on His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder so that you may explain to people﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:44], and His saying: ﴿so that you may explain to them that about which they differ﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:64].

Bundar ibn al-Husayn said: "He is not standing in place of inference; so I made Myself known to you, and I made you independent through knowledge from proofs and evidences." It was also said: "He found you seeking your qibla, lost regarding it, so He guided you to it."

"And He found you poor (ʿāʾilan)": needy, destitute, so He made you rich through the wealth of Khadijah, then through the spoils of war. Muqatil said: "[He made you content] with what He gave you of provision." Ibn al-Sumayqaʿ recited: "wajadaka ʿayyilan" with the yāʾ doubled and without an alif, on the pattern fayʿal, like your saying "ṭāba yaṭību, fa-huwa ṭayyib." From Ibn ʿAtaʾ: "He found you poor in soul." It was also said: "poor in need of Him, so He made you rich through Him." It was also said: "rich through knowledge, poor regarding its rulings, so He made you rich through the rulings of knowledge until your richness was complete for you."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish related to us, from one of them, that he said: "He found you ʿāʾilan" means: you support (taʿūl) creation through knowledge, so He made you rich through the Qur'an, knowledge and wisdom. Al-Akhfash said: "He found you one with dependents (dhā ʿiyāl)." The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Begin with those whom you support." From Ibn ʿAtaʾ: "You had no Book and no Sharia, so He made you rich through both." It was also said: "He found you ʿāʾilan" means: needing the Companions, so He multiplied for you brothers and helpers. The kaf is dropped from His saying "fa-āwā" and its two sisters to match the rhyme of the verse-endings, and because the meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 93, verse 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Meccan, and it has one hundred and seventy-two letters, forty words, and eleven verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Faqih informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Mu'addil narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Mukhalad ibn Abd al-Wahid, from al-Hajjaj ibn Abd Allah, from Abu al-Khalil, from Ali ibn Zayd and Ata' ibn Abi Maymuna, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"Whoever recites the surah Wa al-Duha, he will be among those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is pleased to have intercede for Muhammad, and Allah will record for him ten good deeds for every orphan."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

By the morning brightness (wa al-duha).

The exegetes said: The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Dhu al-Qarnayn, the People of the Cave, and the Spirit. He said: "I will inform you tomorrow," and he did not say, "If Allah wills." So revelation was withheld from him.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: The reason for Jibril's (peace be upon him) delay was that there was a puppy in his house. When Jibril came down to him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rebuked him for his delay, and he said: "O Muhammad, do you not know that we do not enter a house in which there is a dog or a picture?"

They differed concerning the duration of the withholding of revelation from him. Ibn Juraij said: twelve days. Ibn Abbas said: fifteen days. It was said: twenty-five days. Muqatil said: forty days. They said: the polytheists said, "Muhammad's Lord has bid him farewell and abandoned him. If his command were from Allah, revelation would have followed him continuously, as it did with the prophets before him."

The Muslims said: "O Messenger of Allah, does revelation no longer descend upon you?" He said: "How would revelation descend upon me when you do not clean your knuckles nor trim your nails?" Then Allah, glorified is He, sent Jibril (peace be upon him) with this surah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Jibril, you did not come until I longed for you." Jibril (peace be upon him) said: "I was more longing for you, but I am a servant under command, and we do not descend except by the command of your Lord."

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Affan narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, that he heard Jundab ibn Sufyan say: The Prophet (ﷺ) was struck by a stone on his finger, and he said:
"Are you not but a finger that bleeds, and in the way of Allah you have suffered what you have suffered."
Then he remained for two or three nights without standing [in prayer at night]. A woman said to him: "O Muhammad, I do not think your devil has left you. I have not seen him approach you for two or three nights." It was said that the woman who said this was Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: "By the morning brightness." It means the whole day,
and its evidence is His saying: "And by the night when it is still," so He contrasted it with the night. Its parallel is His saying: "that Our punishment comes to them in the forenoon" (duhan), meaning in the daytime. Qatada and Muqatil said: it means the time of forenoon (al-duha), which is the hour when the sun rises high and the day is balanced between heat and cold in winter and summer. It was said: it is the hour in which Allah spoke to Musa. It was said: it is the hour in which the magicians were thrown down prostrate. Its explanation is His saying: "and that the people be gathered in the forenoon." The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said regarding this and similar expressions: it is by supposing a Lord, the meaning being: "and the Lord of the forenoon."

"And by the night when it is still." Al-Hasan said: "it comes with its darkness." This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas; al-Walibi from him: "when it departs." al-Dahhak: "it covers everything." Mujahid, Qatada and Ibn Zayd: "it becomes calm with creation and its darkness settles." It is said: a "night saj" and a "sea saj" when it is still. The rajiz said:
"How good is the moonlit night and the still night, and a path like the cloth of the weaver."

And the poet of Banu Tha'laba said:
"What is our fault if the sea of your cousin's son surges, while your sea is still, hiding nothing of the vanquished?"

"Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He hated you." That is, He has not left you since He chose you, nor has He hated you since He loved you. This is the answer to the oath.

"And the Hereafter is better for you than the first, and your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be satisfied." It was said: of reward; and it was said: of victory, establishment, and the multiplication of believers.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Amir al-Samarqandi informed us, saying: Umar ibn Bahr narrated to us, saying: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Qutayba, from Sufyan, from al-Awza'i, from Isma'il ibn Abd Allah, from Ali ibn Abd Allah ibn Abbas [from his father], who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw what will be opened to my nation after me, victory after victory," and that pleased me. So it was revealed: "And your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be satisfied." He said: "He will give me in Paradise a thousand palaces of pearls, its dust being musk, in each palace what is fitting for him."

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them from Ibn Jarir, who said: Abbad ibn Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: al-Hakam ibn Zahr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "And your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be satisfied," he said: the satisfaction of Muhammad is that no one of his family members enters the Fire. It was also said: it is intercession for all believers.

Abu Abd Allah al-Qanjawi informed me, saying: Abu Ali al-Muqri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Asad al-Mawsili narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Maddadi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us, saying: Harb ibn Surayh al-Bazzaz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: my paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hanafiyya narrated to me, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will intercede for my nation until my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, calls out: 'Are you pleased, O Muhammad?' and I say: 'My Lord, I am pleased.'" Then he said to me: "You people of Iraq say that the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an is: 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah.'" I said: "Indeed, we say that." He said: "But we, the People of the House, say that the most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, Exalted is He, is: 'And your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be satisfied,' and it is intercession."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir ibn Sa'dan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salih al-Misri narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me that Bakr ibn Sawada narrated to him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited Allah's saying concerning Ibrahim: "Whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful," and the saying of Isa: "If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise." Then he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, my nation, my nation," and wept.

Allah, glorified is He, said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad — and your Lord knows best — and ask him what makes him weep." Jibril came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed him. Allah, glorified is He, said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad and say: Indeed We will please you regarding your nation, and We will not grieve you."

It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, when this verse was revealed: "Then I will not be pleased while one of my nation is in the Fire."

Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon Fatima (may Allah be pleased with her), and she was wearing a garment of camel hide, grinding with her hand and nursing her child. The eyes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) shed tears when he saw her, and he said: "O my daughter, hasten the bitterness of this world for the sweetness of the Hereafter, for Allah has revealed to me: 'And your Lord will surely give you, so that you will be satisfied.'"

Then Allah, glorified is He, informed of his state (peace be upon him) before revelation, and reminded him of His blessings, saying, Mighty is He and Exalted: "Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?"

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Nisaburi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Abu Umar al-Hawdi and Abu al-Rabi al-Zahrani narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked my Lord a request that I wished I had not asked. I said: 'O Lord, You gave Sulayman ibn Dawud a great kingdom, and You gave so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such.' He said: 'O Muhammad, did I not find you an orphan and give you refuge?' I said: 'Yes, my Lord.' He said: 'Did I not find you lost and guide you?' I said: 'Yes, my Lord.' He said: 'Did I not find you poor and make you rich?' I said: 'Yes, my Lord.'"

The meaning of the verse: "Did He not find you an orphan": young, poor, weak, when your two parents died, and they had left you no wealth nor shelter. So He made for you a shelter to which you could resort and a dwelling in which you could stay, and He joined you to your uncle Abu Talib until he raised you well and sufficed you in your needs.

I heard the teacher Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Nasr Mansur ibn Abd Allah al-Isfahani say: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Iskandarani say: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Malati say: I heard my father say: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida say: I heard my father say: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq was asked: Why was the Prophet (ﷺ) made an orphan from his parents? He said: "So that there would be no right upon him for any created being."

And I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Anbari relate with a chain of his which I do not remember, from Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, from his father, that he said regarding the Exalted saying: "Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge": it is from the sayings of the Arabs: "a pearl that is unique (durra yatima)" when it has no equal. And it has come in poetry:
"Nor a pearl unique, a sea...
glittering in the merchant's satchel."

So the meaning of the verse is: "Did He not find you unique in your nobility and your virtue, without peer, and so He gave you refuge with Himself."

Ashhab al-Aqili read "fa-awa" with shortening, meaning: "He had mercy on you." The Arabs say: "I gave refuge (awaytu) to so-and-so (li-fulan)," meaning "I had mercy on him."

"And He found you lost," meaning concerning what you are upon today, and He guided you to what you are upon today.

Al-Suddi said: "He was upon the affair of his people for forty years." Al-Kalbi said: "He found you among a misguided people, and guided you to monotheism and prophethood." It was also said: "and He guided them through you." Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Shahr ibn Hawshab and Ibn Kaysan said: "He found you lost (dallan)," from the landmarks of prophethood and the rulings of the Sharia, unaware of them, and He guided you to them. Its parallel and evidence is His saying: "And indeed you were, before it, among the unaware," and His saying: "You did not know what the Book was, nor faith." It was also said: "lost (dallan)" in the valleys of Makkah, and He guided you to your grandfather Abd al-Muttalib and returned you to him.

Abu al-Duha narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got lost while he was a small child in the valleys of Makkah, and Abu Jahl saw him returning from his flocks, and returned him to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib. Allah, glorified is He, bestowed His favor upon him in that, when He returned him to his grandfather by the hand of his enemy.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus informed us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Awf narrated to us, saying: Khalid informed us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Bishr ibn Sa'id, from his father, who said: I performed Hajj in the Jahiliyya, and behold, a man was circumambulating the House, chanting verses and saying:
"O Lord, return my riding camel, Muhammad; return him to me and do me a favor."
I asked: "Who is this?" It was said: "Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim. His camels went astray, and he sent his grandson in search of them, and he never sent him on any errand but that he returned with it, but he was delayed." He said: "I had not gone far when the Prophet (ﷺ) came with the camels, and he said: 'O my son, I have grieved over you with a grief that will never leave me.'"

And in the hadith of Ka'b al-Ahbar concerning the birth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the beginning of his affair: when Halima had fulfilled the duty of nursing, she brought the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to return him to Abd al-Muttalib. Halima said: "I set out walking until I reached the great gate of the gates of Makkah, and I heard a caller calling: 'Congratulations to you, O valley of Makkah! Today the light, the religion, the splendor and the beauty will return to you.'" She said: "Then I set down the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to attend to a need and fix my clothes, and I heard a severe crash. I turned and did not see him, so I said: 'O people, where is the boy?' They said: 'Which of the boys?'"

I said: "Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, by whom Allah brightened my face and enriched my poverty. I raised him until, when I attained in him my joy and hope, I came to return him, and this one takes from my trust, snatched from before my eyes before his foot touched the ground. By al-Lat and al-Uzza, if I do not see him I will throw myself from the top of the mountain, and I will surely cut myself into pieces."

They said: "We have seen nothing." When they despaired of me, I put my hand on the top of my head and said: "Alas Muhammad! Alas my son!" The virgin girls wept at my weeping, and the people cried out with me in grief for me. Then behold, an old man like a withered one leaning on a staff said: "What is wrong with you, O Sa'diyya?"

I said: "I have lost my son Muhammad." He said: "Do not weep. I will direct you to one who knows his knowledge, and if he wishes to return him, he will do so." I said: "May my soul be your ransom, and who is he?" He said: "The greatest idol, Hubal."

She said: He entered and I was watching. He circumambulated Hubal, kissed its head and called out: "O my master! Your favor upon Quraysh has been ancient, and this Sa'diyya claims that a son of hers has gone astray, so return him if you wish, and remove this desolation from the valley of Makkah, for she claims that her son Muhammad has gone astray." He said: Hubal fell on its face, and the idols toppled, and it said: "Away from us, O old man! Our destruction is at the hand of Muhammad."

She said: Then the old man came, and I heard the chattering of his teeth and the trembling of his knee, and he had thrown his staff from his hand, saying: "O Halima, your son has a Lord who will not neglect him, so seek him gently." She said: I feared the news would reach Abd al-Muttalib before me, so I went to him. When he looked at me he said: "Did a fortunate one come to you, or an unlucky one?" I said: "Rather, the greatest misfortune." He understood it from me and said: "Perhaps your son went astray from you." I said: "Yes." He supposed that some of Quraysh had seized him. Abd al-Muttalib drew his sword, no one could stand before him from the intensity of his anger, and he called out at the top of his voice: "O family of Ghalib, O family of Ghalib!" — and this was their call in the Jahiliyya — and all of Quraysh answered him, and they said: "What is your story?" He said: "My son Muhammad is lost." Quraysh said: "Mount, and we will mount with you. If you climb a mountain, we will climb it with you; if you plunge into a sea, we will plunge with you." He mounted, Quraysh mounted with him, and he took the high part of Makkah and descended to its low part. When he saw nothing, he left the people, wrapped himself and donned another garment, and came to the Sacred House. He circumambulated seven times, then began to say:
"O Lord, return my riding camel Muhammad; return him, my Lord, and do me a favor.
O Lord, Muhammad has not been found, the gathering of my people all scattered."

Then we heard a caller calling from the air: "O people, do not cry out, for Muhammad has a Lord who will not forsake him or neglect him." Abd al-Muttalib said: "O you who call, who is with us, and where is he?" He said: "In the valley of Tihama, by the tree of Yemen."

Abd al-Muttalib came mounted and armed. When he reached part of the way, Waraqa ibn Nawfal met him, and they went together. While they were thus, behold, the Prophet (ﷺ) was standing under a tree, pulling its branches and playing with its leaves. Abd al-Muttalib said to him: "Who are you, boy?"

He said: "I am Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib." Abd al-Muttalib said: "May my soul be your ransom, I am your grandfather." Then he carried him on the front of his saddle and returned him to Makkah, and Quraysh were reassured after that.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out with his uncle Abu Talib in the caravan of Maysara, the slave of Khadija. While he was riding one dark night on a camel, Iblis came, seized the camel's reins, and turned him away from the road. Then Jibril came, blew upon Iblis a blast by which he fell as far as Abyssinia, and returned him to the caravan. Allah bestowed His favor upon him in that.

It was said: "And He found you lost" refers to the night of the Ascension, when Jibril left you and you did not know the way, and He guided you to the lote-tree of the Throne.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish narrated to me, saying: Some people of theology said regarding His saying:

And He found you lost and guided you: when the Arabs find a tree alone in a wilderness of the earth, with no second one beside it, they call it "ḍāllah" (a lone tree), and they find their way to the road by it.

He said: "And He found you lost and guided you" means: alone, with no prophet other than you, so I guided the creation to Me through you. ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Tirmidhi said: "And He found you obscure, not mentioned and not known, who you were, so He guided them to you until they knew you, and informed them of what He had bestowed upon you."

Bassam ibn ʿAbdullah said: "And He found you lost" means: lost regarding yourself, not knowing who you were, so He made you know yourself and your state. Abu Bakr al-Warraq and others said: "And He found you lost" means: lost in love for Abu Talib, so He guided you to love of Him. Others said: "He found you loving, so He guided you to the One you love." The evidence for this is His saying, relating of the brothers of Joseph: ﴿Indeed, our father is in clear error﴾ [Surah Yusuf 12:8], and His saying: ﴿By Allah, you are surely in your old error﴾ [Surah Yusuf 12:95], meaning: the excess of love for Joseph.

It was also said: "We found you forgetful regarding the matter of the exception (istithna')" when you were asked about the People of the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿that one of them may forget (tadilla) [the other]﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 2:282], meaning: forget. Sahl said: "He found your self to be the self of desire and nature, so He turned it toward the path of knowledge and the Sharia." Junayd said: "He found you perplexed regarding the explanation of the Book revealed to you, so He guided you to its explanation," based on His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder so that you may explain to people﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:44], and His saying: ﴿so that you may explain to them that about which they differ﴾ [Surah al-Nahl 16:64].

Bundar ibn al-Husayn said: "He is not standing in place of inference; so I made Myself known to you, and I made you independent through knowledge from proofs and evidences." It was also said: "He found you seeking your qibla, lost regarding it, so He guided you to it."

"And He found you poor (ʿāʾilan)": needy, destitute, so He made you rich through the wealth of Khadijah, then through the spoils of war. Muqatil said: "[He made you content] with what He gave you of provision." Ibn al-Sumayqaʿ recited: "wajadaka ʿayyilan" with the yāʾ doubled and without an alif, on the pattern fayʿal, like your saying "ṭāba yaṭību, fa-huwa ṭayyib." From Ibn ʿAtaʾ: "He found you poor in soul." It was also said: "poor in need of Him, so He made you rich through Him." It was also said: "rich through knowledge, poor regarding its rulings, so He made you rich through the rulings of knowledge until your richness was complete for you."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Habish related to us, from one of them, that he said: "He found you ʿāʾilan" means: you support (taʿūl) creation through knowledge, so He made you rich through the Qur'an, knowledge and wisdom. Al-Akhfash said: "He found you one with dependents (dhā ʿiyāl)." The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Begin with those whom you support." From Ibn ʿAtaʾ: "You had no Book and no Sharia, so He made you rich through both." It was also said: "He found you ʿāʾilan" means: needing the Companions, so He multiplied for you brothers and helpers. The kaf is dropped from His saying "fa-āwā" and its two sisters to match the rhyme of the verse-endings, and because the meaning is well known.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 93, verses 9–11:**

﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾. And remember your own orphanhood. Al-Nakha'i and al-Sha'bi recited *fa-la takkahr* (فلا تكهر) with the letter *kaf* (ك). It is also so in the *Mushaf* (the codex, the written copy of the Qur'an) of Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud). The Arabs interchange the *qaf* (ق) and the *kaf* (ك) (*ta'aqub*, the alternation of sounds). This is shown by the hadith of Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam, who spoke during the prayer and said: "He did not frown at me (*ma kahharani*) nor strike me."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying:

Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to us, from Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dayli, who said: I heard Abu al-Ghayth narrate, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who cares for an orphan, whether his own or another's, shall be with me and him in Paradise like these two, if he fears Allah, the Glorified." [168] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/375.]] And Malik indicated with the index and middle fingers.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn [Yusuf] [[He is Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik.]] narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Nasr al-Tusi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl narrated to us at Ra's al-Ayn, saying: Ibrahim ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, saying:

al-Husayn ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Ali, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the orphan weeps, the Throne of the Merciful trembles at his weeping. Then Allah, the Glorified, says to His angels: 'O My angels! Who has made this orphan weep, the one whose father has been hidden in the dust?' The angels say: 'Our Lord, You know best.' Allah says: 'O My angels! I call you to witness that for whoever quiets him and pleases him, I shall please him on the Day of Resurrection.'" So Umar, whenever he saw an orphan, would wipe his head and give him something. [169] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/101.]]

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed me, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Amr narrated to us, from Abu Hazm, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Whoever takes in an orphan and is responsible for his maintenance and provides for his needs, it will be for him a barrier from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever wipes the head of an orphan, for every hair (that his hand passes over) there will be a good deed for him.

﴿And as for the one who asks, do not drive him away﴾. That is, do not rebuke him; rather, speak to him gently and kindly, and remember your own poverty.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, with what he permitted me to narrate from him, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Hulwani informed us, saying: al-Abbas ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id Abu Amr al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Aslam al-Anbari narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying, the Glorified and Exalted: ﴿And as for the one who asks, do not drive him away﴾. He said: "As for him, he is not the beggar who comes to you; rather, he is the seeker of knowledge."

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed me, saying: al-Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Qawhiyal [[Perhaps: Ibn Mawhar, Qawhiyar.]] narrated to me, saying:

Hatim ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ubayd ibn Nu'aysh narrated to me, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Adam say: "﴿And as for the one who asks, do not drive him away﴾." He said: "When the seeker of knowledge comes to you, do not drive him away."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Abu Aruba narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hakim and al-Husayn ibn Salama ibn Abi Kabsha narrated to us, both saying: Abu Qutayba narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Hashimi narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you be prevented by the beggar from giving to him when he asks, even if he sees on his hand two golden bracelets (*qulbayn*)." [170] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 6/407, no. 16289. The qulb is a bracelet.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanba narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Kisa'i narrated to us, saying:

Ahmad ibn Thabit ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Shammas narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ayyub al-Dabbi narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Adham, who said: "How excellent are the beggars! They carry our provision to the Hereafter."

Ibrahim also said: "The beggar seeks the Hereafter; he comes to the door of one of you and says: 'Will you send anything to your family?'"

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Zakariyya al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Hudba ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Subban ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Talha ibn Amr narrated to us, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you have turned away the beggar three times and he has not returned, there is no blame on you if you rebuke him." [171] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 6/400, no. 16253. al-Zabr means rebuke and prevention.]]

﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾. That is, prophethood, according to Mujahid, Ibn Abi Najih, from him (Ibn Abbas), who said: "It is the Qur'an," and al-Kalbi also held this view. The ruling of the verse is general, covering all favours.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: al-Qatay'i narrated to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal narrated to me, saying: Abu Amr al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, saying: Nasr ibn Ali narrated to me, saying:

Abd Allah ibn Ghalib used to say every morning: "Allah has given me good last night: I recited such-and-such, prayed such-and-such, remembered Allah such-and-such, and did such-and-such." It was said to him: "O Abu Firas, a person like you should not say such a thing." He replied: "Allah, the Glorified, says: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾. And you say: 'Do not proclaim the blessing of your Lord.'"

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: Shabr ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'mar narrated to us, from Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever is given some good and does not see it upon himself, will be named by Allah 'the hater of His blessings' (*baghid Allah*, one hated by Allah) and an enemy to His favours." [172] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/102; al-Shukr li-Allah of Ibn Abi al-Dunya: 92.]]

We were informed by al-Hasan, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn Mani' narrated to us, saying: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, that is al-Qasim ibn al-Walid, from al-Sha'bi, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say from the pulpit: "Whoever does not give thanks for little will not give thanks for much; whoever does not give thanks to people has not given thanks to Allah. Speaking of Allah's blessing is thankfulness, and leaving it is disbelief. Community is mercy and division is punishment." [173] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/278.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: Shabr ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'mar narrated to us, from Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 93, verses 9–11:**

﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾. And remember your own orphanhood. Al-Nakha'i and al-Sha'bi recited *fa-la takkahr* (فلا تكهر) with the letter *kaf* (ك). It is also so in the *Mushaf* (the codex, the written copy of the Qur'an) of Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud). The Arabs interchange the *qaf* (ق) and the *kaf* (ك) (*ta'aqub*, the alternation of sounds). This is shown by the hadith of Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam, who spoke during the prayer and said: "He did not frown at me (*ma kahharani*) nor strike me."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying:

Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to us, from Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dayli, who said: I heard Abu al-Ghayth narrate, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who cares for an orphan, whether his own or another's, shall be with me and him in Paradise like these two, if he fears Allah, the Glorified." [168] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/375.]] And Malik indicated with the index and middle fingers.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn [Yusuf] [[He is Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik.]] narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Nasr al-Tusi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl narrated to us at Ra's al-Ayn, saying: Ibrahim ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, saying:

al-Husayn ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Ali, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the orphan weeps, the Throne of the Merciful trembles at his weeping. Then Allah, the Glorified, says to His angels: 'O My angels! Who has made this orphan weep, the one whose father has been hidden in the dust?' The angels say: 'Our Lord, You know best.' Allah says: 'O My angels! I call you to witness that for whoever quiets him and pleases him, I shall please him on the Day of Resurrection.'" So Umar, whenever he saw an orphan, would wipe his head and give him something. [169] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/101.]]

Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed me, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Amr narrated to us, from Abu Hazm, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Whoever takes in an orphan and is responsible for his maintenance and provides for his needs, it will be for him a barrier from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever wipes the head of an orphan, for every hair (that his hand passes over) there will be a good deed for him.

﴿And as for the one who asks, do not drive him away﴾. That is, do not rebuke him; rather, speak to him gently and kindly, and remember your own poverty.

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, with what he permitted me to narrate from him, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Hulwani informed us, saying: al-Abbas ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id Abu Amr al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Aslam al-Anbari narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying, the Glorified and Exalted: ﴿And as for the one who asks, do not drive him away﴾. He said: "As for him, he is not the beggar who comes to you; rather, he is the seeker of knowledge."

Hatim ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ubayd ibn Nu'aysh narrated to me, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Adam say: "﴿And as for the one who asks, do not drive him away﴾." He said: "When the seeker of knowledge comes to you, do not drive him away."
